tb21_profile.skill: Cryptanalytic parameter recovery from a black box: design queries to a scalar-valued piecewise-linear function, use finite differences to find where each hidden ReLU switches, infer the unknown hidden width, and reconstruct the first-layer weight matrix up to neuron permutation and per-row scaling.
tb21_profile.domain: NumPy numerical linear algebra and floating-point probing; neural networks; black-box / model-extraction attacks.
tb21_profile.task_form: Reverse-engineer-a-black-box plus implement-an-algorithm-from-its-description, delivering a script that re-derives the answer dynamically and is graded up to an equivalence class.

verifier_notes: No grade overturned. Nothing FREE made any list for this task - the CalibForge mathematics cluster is uniformly ok/strong, so the hard rule never bound here. Worth flagging that mathematics_20260604_003814_004 is only graded 'ok' while being the single closest candidate in the whole pool; its test compares reconstructed function values within 1e-4 on fresh inputs, which is a real check, so the grade understates it.

notes: CalibForge is not merely the best pool here, it contains what is effectively the same task: mathematics_20260604_003814_004 imports forward.py, takes a 10-dimensional numpy input, returns one float, asks for a script literally named /app/steal.py, and wants the hidden a_j vectors of a sum of |a_j.x + b_j| with an unknown number of terms. Around it sits a whole family of black-box parameter-recovery tasks (matrix up to row permutation, unknown-rank matrix under a query budget, unknown internal dimension, sum of exponentials with unknown k, sparse polynomial interpolation, GMM from log_prob) that between them cover every subproblem this task has. Seven of the final ten come from that one cluster and none of it was in the retrieved shortlist for this task - the whole cluster was found with a regex for black-box and recover the parameters. TMax contributes its oracle-probing tasks, which teach the same probe-infer-reimplement-exactly discipline in a shell/CLI setting rather than a numerical one. Terminal-Lego, Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld are all weak: Lego has scattered numpy exercises (implementing numpy.gradient from scratch is its best), TerminalWorld's only real match is a timing side-channel password recovery, and Recursive-Task-Synthesis has essentially nothing - its bottom half is quota filler at overall 1-2. SWE-Rebench is better than its task_form suggests, with pennylane-2057 (second derivative wrong exactly at zero) sitting right on this task's central numerical hazard.
